fields.name: value
fields.text: The other character in the relationship.
fields.values: a character, such as a saved scope or a link

label: Has selected mandate
summary: Whether the given mandate was the one selected for the diarch.
details: Works even when there is no active diarchy. The documented example runs it on the diarch, written as `scope:diarch = { has_selected_mandate = live_long_and_prosper }`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The mandate to check for.
fields.values: a mandate key

label: Sexuality
summary: Whether the character's sexuality is the given one.
details: `none` is the value for characters who have no sexuality yet, such as children. The other values are heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual and asexual.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The sexuality to check for.
fields.values: heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual, asexual or none

label: Top phase parameter
summary: Whether the situation's top sub-region currently has the given phase parameter.
details: The game's documentation does not define phase parameters; vanilla's values look like named flags of a situation phase. Vanilla uses it mostly with church parameters, for example the investiture controversy.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The parameter name to look for.
fields.values: a phase parameter key

label: Has spawned court events
summary: Whether the character has court events that are shown in the royal court view, opened or not.
details: Only works on player characters that have a royal court. Vanilla only ever uses it as `no`.

label: Has special building
summary: Whether the province (holding) has a special building.
details: Written as `yes` or `no`.

label: Has special building slot
summary: Whether the province (holding) has a slot for a special building.
details: Written as `yes` or `no`. Vanilla only uses it as `no`.

label: Has special character
summary: Whether the faction has a special character assigned.
details: Written as `yes` or `no`. The game's documentation does not say what makes a character special; vanilla has no use of it in the input.

label: Has special title
summary: Whether the faction has a special title assigned.
details: Written as `yes` or `no`. The game's documentation does not say what makes a title special; vanilla has no use of it in the input.

label: Has fulfillment type
summary: Whether the character uses the given spiritual fulfillment type.
details: Vanilla only uses `christian_fulfillment`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The spiritual fulfillment type to check for.
fields.values: a spiritual fulfillment type key

label: Has stationed regiment
summary: Whether the province has any regiments stationed in it.
details: Written as `yes` or `no`. Vanilla only uses it as `yes`.

label: Has stationed regiment type
summary: Whether the province has a stationed regiment of the given base type.
details: Vanilla uses base types such as skirmishers, pikemen, archers, heavy_infantry, light_cavalry, heavy_cavalry, archer_cavalry and camel_cavalry.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The base type of regiment.
fields.values: a base regiment type key

label: Strong claim on
summary: Whether the character has an explicit pressed claim (a strong claim) on the given title.
details: The game's documentation calls it an explicit pressed claim. A separate trigger, `has_strong_implicit_claim_on`, checks the implicit kind.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The title the claim is on.
fields.values: a title, such as a saved scope, a link or `title:k_asturias`

label: Strong hook on
summary: Whether the character holds a strong hook (a strong lever of influence) on the given character.
details: The game's documentation of `has_strong_usable_hook` adds that the hook must not be on cooldown, which implies this one does not demand that. To require a usable hook, use that trigger.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The character the hook is held on.
fields.values: a character, such as a saved scope or a link

label: Strong implicit claim on
summary: Whether the character has an implicit pressed claim on the given title.
details: The game's documentation says only "implicit" and does not explain what makes a claim implicit. The explicit kind is checked with `has_strong_claim_on`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The title the claim is on.
fields.values: a title, such as a saved scope or a link

label: Usable strong hook on
summary: Whether the character holds a strong hook on the given character that is not on cooldown.
details: Compared with `has_strong_hook`, this one also requires the hook to be off cooldown.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The character the hook is held on.
fields.values: a character, such as a saved scope or a link

label: Phase parameter
summary: Whether the struggle's current phase has the given parameter.
details: It can only check parameters that are yes/no flags.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The parameter name to look for.
fields.values: a phase parameter key

label: Phase parameter
summary: Whether the situation sub-region has the given phase parameter.
details: Vanilla uses it with parameters of the great steppe situation, for example the one for cheaper hunts.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The parameter name to look for.
fields.values: a phase parameter key

label: Has subject contract group
summary: Whether the character has a subject contract of the given group.
details: The documented example is `scope:actor = { has_contract_group = { contract_group = <key> } }`, which differs from this key's name and form. Vanilla uses this key with a plain name, such as tributary_mandala.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The contract group.
fields.values: a subject contract group key

label: Has appointment investors
summary: Whether the character has any investors for their appointment towards the given title.
details: The documented example is `scope:character = { has_succession_appointment_investors = scope:title }`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The title the appointment is for.
fields.values: a title, such as a saved scope

label: Has targeting faction
summary: Whether there is a faction aimed at the character.
details: Written as `yes` or `no`. Vanilla uses it as `yes`.

label: Task contract group
summary: Whether the task contract belongs to the given group.
details: It runs on a task contract. The documented example puts it under a character scope, which does not match; vanilla's only value is admin_governance_group.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The contract group.
fields.values: a task contract group key

label: Task contract type
summary: Whether the task contract is of the given type.
details: It runs on a task contract, as in `scope:task_contract = { has_task_contract_type = type_name }`.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The contract type.
fields.values: a task contract type key

label: Has tax collector
summary: Whether the tax slot has a tax collector employed.
details: Written as `yes` or `no`. Works on a tax slot.

label: Has tenet
summary: Whether the faith has the given tenet.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The tenet to check for.
fields.values: a tenet key

label: Tenet status
summary: Whether the rite holds exactly the given stance on the given tenet.
details: Only an exact match counts. Rites can only override the faith's core tenets, and a faith's core tenets count as permitted for the rite.

fields.name: tenet
fields.text: The tenet to check.
fields.values: a tenet key, a saved scope or `prev`

fields.name: status
fields.text: The stance the rite holds on the tenet.
fields.values: unknown, known, prohibited, permitted or core

label: Holds a title
summary: Whether the character holds the given title.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The title to check for.
fields.values: a title, such as `title:e_byzantium` or a saved scope

label: Has title law
summary: Whether the title has the given title-specific law.
details: Vanilla uses it with succession laws such as scandinavian_elective_succession_law and male_preference_law.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The law to check for.
fields.values: a title law key

label: Has title law flag
summary: Whether the title has a title-specific law with the given flag.
details: Vanilla uses flags such as elective_succession_law and advanced_succession_law.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The flag to look for.
fields.values: a law flag name

label: Tradition category
summary: Whether the culture tradition belongs to the given category.
details: Vanilla uses the categories regional, realm, combat, societal and ritual.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The category to check for.
fields.values: regional, realm, combat, societal or ritual

label: Has trait
summary: Whether the character has the given trait, or any trait of the given trait group.
details: Vanilla uses it more than 22,000 times. The value can also be a saved scope.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The trait or trait group.
fields.values: a trait key or trait group key
